c1-31-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Fear and Decisions
c1-31-01.scenario: A friend has read about Bibó István and asks what fear does to a community.
c1-31-01.prompt: Tell your friend what a community may do when it is guided by fear, and that the decision was not made out of conviction.
cues: Say what fear does to a community's decisions
Say that the decision was made for political reasons
c1-31-01.target: Félelemtől vezérelve a közösség könnyen téves döntéseket hoz. Nem meggyőződésből, hanem politikai okból döntöttek így.
c1-31-01.english: Guided by fear, a community easily makes wrong decisions. They decided so not out of conviction but for political reasons.
c1-31-01.canDo: I can say what drives a community with *félelemtől vezérelve* or *politikai okból*.

c1-31-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Is to Blame?
c1-31-02.scenario: A friend asks you what is wrong with stories that put the blame on someone else.
c1-31-02.prompt: Tell your friend what a community that looks for a scapegoat does not do, and why a story that puts the responsibility on others is not complete.
cues: Say what a community that looks for a scapegoat does not face
Say what is wrong with a story that puts the responsibility on others
c1-31-02.target: A bűnbakot kereső közösség nem néz szembe a saját hibáival. A felelősséget másra hárító történet kényelmes, de nem teljes.
c1-31-02.english: A community that looks for a scapegoat does not face its own mistakes. A story that puts the responsibility on someone else is comfortable but not complete.
c1-31-02.canDo: I can describe a story or a community with a participle before the noun, as in *a felelősséget másra hárító történet*.

c1-31-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Facts, Not Fear
c1-31-03.scenario: A friend asks you what a community can do instead of looking for a scapegoat.
c1-31-03.prompt: Tell your friend what the community does instead of looking for a scapegoat, and that some react with fear while others examine the facts.
cues: Say what they do instead of looking for a scapegoat
c1-31-03.target: Ahelyett, hogy bűnbakot keresnének, megvizsgálják a tényeket. Míg egyesek félelmükben bűnbakot keresnek, mások a tényeket vizsgálják.
c1-31-03.english: Instead of looking for a scapegoat, they examine the facts. While some look for a scapegoat out of fear, others examine the facts.
c1-31-03.canDo: I can contrast two reactions to fear with *míg* and *nem …, hanem …*.

c1-31-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Open the Archive?
c1-31-04.scenario: A friend asks you why people want to open an archive and why the truth should be stated.
c1-31-04.prompt: Tell your friend why the archive is opened and why the truth is stated.
cues: Give the purpose of opening the archive
Give the purpose of stating the truth
c1-31-04.target: Annak érdekében nyitják meg a levéltárat, hogy a kutatók megismerjék a múltat. Kimondjuk az igazságot, nehogy a hazugság váljon közös emlékké.
c1-31-04.english: The archive is opened so that researchers can come to know the past. We state the truth so that the lie does not become a shared memory.
c1-31-04.canDo: I can give the purpose of an action with *annak érdekében, hogy*.

c1-31-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What Bibó Studied
c1-31-05.scenario: A friend who has read about Bibó István asks when he wrote his study and what fear does to a community.
c1-31-05.prompt: Tell your friend when Bibó wrote the study and what fear does to a community's sense of reality.
cues: Say when Bibó wrote the study
Say how much fear distorts the sense of reality
c1-31-05.target: Bibó István 1946-ban írta A kelet-európai kisállamok nyomorúsága című tanulmányát. A félelem számottevően torzítja a valóságérzéket.
c1-31-05.english: Bibó István wrote his study The Misery of the Small States of Eastern Europe in 1946. Fear markedly distorts the sense of reality.
c1-31-05.canDo: I can say how much fear changes a community with *számottevően* or *alapjaiban*.

c1-31-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Unit
c1-31-consolidation.scenario: At the end of a talk about Bibó István, a friend asks what you learned about fear and memory.
c1-31-consolidation.prompt: Tell your friend what fear does to a community, what a community that looks for a scapegoat does not face, and why archives are opened.
cues: Say what fear does to the sense of reality
Say what a community that looks for a scapegoat does not face
Say why the archive is opened
c1-31-consolidation.target: A félelem számottevően torzítja a valóságérzéket. A bűnbakot kereső közösség nem néz szembe a saját hibáival. Annak érdekében nyitják meg a levéltárat, hogy a kutatók megismerjék a múltat.
c1-31-consolidation.english: Fear markedly distorts the sense of reality. A community that looks for a scapegoat does not face its own mistakes. The archive is opened so that researchers can come to know the past.
c1-31-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words of historical trauma, responsibility and working through the past.
